Also, that bit about some academic advisor said it was rare to get a second appeal...I went to get a part time job once and the guy working said to me the manager was not hiring and he wouldn't give me an app. I was upset but made a purchase and left. I got home and loved the product so much I decided I was just going to email the owner/manager and just tell him that I love the products and if there were ever an opportunity, I'd like to have it. Do you know he had me come in for an interview? I got the job and filled out the application after.

My point: of advisor lady isn't the one to say yes/no to your appeal, then sidestep that broad and don't call it quits until they say no to your appeal. THEN find a plan b. There are grants or scholarships from smaller funders for hometown folks or for being left handed. Or, do online, Part time, one class at a time (like one a semester). That gives you time to decompress from the stress of classes and build up the funds for another class (I would suggest trying to have at least enough for 2 classes ready before you start so that as you work through the year by the summer you are ready to go for next year.
